blocks.text: BRUSSELS, Belgium — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders Friday to keep financing Kyiv’s fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, as he insisted he was standing up for his country amid a fresh row with US President Donald Trump. Kyiv’s ties with Trump have nosedived after the US leader eased sanctions on Russia as part of a deal to supply diesel. Trump branded Kyiv’s actions a “disgrace” and said it was easier to deal with Russia’s President Vladimir Putin than Zelensky, after the Ukrainian leader ordered his forces to resume strikes on Russian refineries. “I defend the interests […]...
